title: Predictive holdback routing and graceful spill to cold pools
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Under transient spikes our dedicated GPU pools see short-lived bursts that cause headroom collapse and long tail latency. Existing admission controls either shed aggressively (losing work) or queue indefinitely (increasing latency and consuming resources). Goal: implement a predictive holdback routing layer that briefly delays a calibrated fraction of incoming requests based on short-term traffic forecasts and SLO targets, and when sustained overload is detected, spill excess requests to a configurable cold-pool or low-priority fleet with soft degradation guarantees. The feature should maintain per-tenant throughput guarantees while minimizing dropped work and keeping 99th percentile latency within SLA targets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic spike tests (2-5x baseline for 30s), p99 token-latency increases no more than 30% compared to steady-state and success rate >= 99.5% for P0 tenants.
2) System routes predicted-excess requests to cold-pool when predicted sustained overload > 20s; configuration flag to adjust threshold per-tenant.
3) Rollback toggle available: feature can be disabled cluster-wide within 60s without requiring service restart.
4) Metrics emitted: predicted_holdback_ratio, spill_rate_per_tenant, cold_pool_accept_rate, grace_eviction_count; dashboards created in Console.
5) End-to-end tests validate that cached KV lookups and streaming responses survive spillover path with no silent failures.
6) Documentation and SDK examples updated to show per-tenant holdback controls and cold-pool routing policy.
design_notes: Predictive model: use a short-window exponential moving average + derivative to estimate imminent load; conservative bias to avoid oscillation.
Holdback decision: compute per-tenant holdback probability p = clamp(alpha*(predicted_load - capacity)/capacity, 0, max_holdback) where alpha is tunable per-tenant.
Routing paths: primary (dedicated pool), soft-holdback (delay queue with early-bailouts), cold-pool spill (lower-cost fleet with reduced SLOs), and drop path as last resort for emergency pressure.
Queueing mechanics: implement a bounded delay-queue with token refresh and backpressure to upstream ingress; timeouts propagate canonical error codes to callers.
Integration: admission layer lives in the routing proxy (edge) and publishes decisions to the control-plane for visibility. Autoscaler signals capacity changes used by predictor.
Consistency: prioritize tenant throughput guarantees by reserving a minimal always-available slot fraction and calibrating holdback per SLA tier.
Cold-pool contract: accept requests with lower concurrency and a configurable quality-degrade hint (e.g., smaller response length, lower model variant) propagated to runtime.
Fallback: when cold-pool is full, policy can demote to reduced-generation or enqueue with exponential backoff depending on tenant policy.
Operational safety: provide rate-limiter cap and circuit-breaker that opens when cold-pool error rate crosses threshold; circuit auto-closes after cooldown.
Data plane telemetry: include sampling of routed request traces, latencies, and cause tags (predicted-holdback, spill, dropped) for regression debugging.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind runtime toggle; default off in production clusters.
2) Canary in a non-critical region with 5% of traffic and a single tenant with synthetic load patterns.
3) Expand to 20% traffic and two additional tenants, monitor p99 latency and spill metrics for 48h.
4) Open beta for customers with dedicated pools and opt-in via Console knob; collect feedback and tweak alpha/max_holdback.
5) Full launch for all dedicated clusters after 4 weeks of stable canary metrics and after automated chaos tests.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-tenant holdback ratio, spill rate, cold-pool latency distribution, dropped count, predictor error (predicted vs observed).
SLO alerts: p99 latency > SLA for 10m -> page; cold-pool error rate > 1% for 5m -> page.
Health checks: cold-pool capacity low (<= 5% spare) -> warn; predictor divergence > 40% -> warn and auto-disable holdbacks for safety.
Audit logs: record decisionReason for any spill/delay/drop for compliance and postmortems.
testing: Load tests: driver that replays production ingress patterns and injects controlled spikes to validate holdback and spillover behavior.
Chaos tests: kill cold-pool nodes and verify circuit-breaker and fallback policies operate without data loss.
Integration tests: end-to-end smoke for streaming, KV cache hits across spill path, and correct propagation of quality-degrade hints.
Unit tests: predictor math, holdback probability bounds, and admission policy decision matrix.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: inaccurate prediction causes unnecessary holds and degrades perceived capacity. Mitigation: conservative tuning, short smoothing windows, and canary with synthetic load.
Risk: cold-pool compatibility issues (models or quantization mismatches). Mitigation: enforce model compatibility checks and offer automatic fallback variants with documented quality differences.
Risk: complexity increases debugging time for incidents. Mitigation: rich telemetry, decisionReason tags, and runbook additions.
